subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should embedded helper runs consume a reusable prepared CLI-dispatch plan, or should callers permanently opt into the new `subscription-auth` mode with `claude-cli`-specific credential policy?
rationale: Both designs can fix this recall failure, but choosing the permanent owner of provider resolution, credential selection, timeout budgeting, and capability policy affects other helper paths and cannot safely be inferred from this one caller.

options.title: Use a prepared dispatch plan
options.body: Resolve backend capability and credential mode once at the agent-runtime boundary, then reuse that decision for timeout budgeting and execution across helper callers.

options.title: Keep caller opt-in
options.body: Retain the new active-memory opt-in and hardcoded Claude policy, accepting a parallel helper-routing contract that future callers must adopt individually.

recommendation.title: Use a prepared dispatch plan
recommendation.body: Resolve backend capability and credential mode once at the agent-runtime boundary, then reuse that decision for timeout budgeting and execution across helper callers.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman owns the merged Active Memory behavior and is the strongest available history-backed person to coordinate the recall-side contract with an agent-runtime reviewer.
